# SAS & GrowthBook | Enterprise Evaluation
Date: 2026-09-23 | Duration: 48m

## Summary
The organization has used self-hosted GrowthBook for more than two years for organization-wide feature toggling and extensive server- and client-side experimentation, without DOM manipulation. The discussion covered enterprise benefits including SSO, SAML, role-based access, multi-organization separation, granular project permissions, customer success, training, onboarding, and support for multiple teams. Advanced capabilities include Cubed post-stratification, sequential testing, custom dashboards, query optimization, deeper behavioral insights, AI-assisted learnings, safe rollouts, automatic flag disabling after performance drops, namespace separation, and contextual bandits for adaptive traffic allocation. JIRA integration is available through webhooks, while the visual editor has limitations with Next.js hydration and is recommended for development environments. Commercial options include pricing by user seat or annual experiment count, with flexible tiering, and a proof of concept offering live access, onboarding, and support. Marcel will send a recap and commercial range information, and a follow-up will include Trills and Claudia.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Enterprise, Experimentation, Self-hosted, Feature Toggles, JIRA Integration

## Action Items
**Rémy Marin**

Send JIRA integration setup documentation (13:00)  
Provide visual editor DOM handling info (16:27)  
Share video and materials on contextual bandits (28:20)  
Assist with feature deep dives and clarifications (36:39)  

**Marcel Geldner**  
Send email recap with GrowthBook Enterprise info (30:00)  
Share proof of concept details and contract constraints (36:20)  
Provide calendar link for follow-up meeting (37:50)

Provide SAS budget timeline and procurement thresholds (33:46)

# SAS & Growthbook | Enterprise Setup (POC) + Commercials
Date: 2026-10-02 | Duration: 39.619998931884766m

## Summary
GrowthBook has been used for two years with stable adoption and few technical concerns, but the organization wants to strengthen its experimentation culture through better processes, analytics, personalization, and controlled test growth. Improving the currently low conversion rate, which varies between 2% and 3% by segment, is a priority, alongside clearer alignment on key metrics. Scaling requires enterprise governance, including role-based permissions, infrastructure clarity, internal data integrations, and more understanding of JIRA usage. Funnel analytics, user journeys, contextual bandits, and AI-powered insights were discussed as tools for analyzing behavior, allocating traffic, evaluating significance, and suggesting next steps. Contentful is the CMS across markets and languages, with GrowthBook integration possible through its API and SDK, although Redis and Cloudflare caching may interfere with tests. Costs remain under review because CDN and bandwidth expenses are unclear and potentially substantial, while GrowthBook offers a flat enterprise fee that includes CDN traffic and pricing based on user seats. Further architecture discussions, cost clarification, shared materials, and a follow-up meeting were proposed.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, experimentation culture, enterprise integration, A/B testing, Contentful integration, contextual bandits

## Action Items
**Rémy Marin**  
Support training on GrowthBook funnel (13:28)  
Provide guidance on GrowthBook Contentful integration (26:00)
